title: Handoff, Pictures, Approvals
eyebrow: Design · saved work no other folder can erase, pictures that always show, approvals that always register

short.lead: The desktop retest found a way to lose work. Every folder on a branch saves to the same place on GitHub, the ref refs/house-rules/autosave/<branch>. Desktop session A saved an uncommitted line there as snapshot e724bf2. Then a session in a second clone of the same branch (call it clone B), which had none of that work, saved its own state to that same place as snapshot 32fb8c8. That replaced A's snapshot. The pickup, which shows saved work when a session starts, now finds nothing to restore. A's line still exists, but only in clone A's folder and in a local copy of the old snapshot in this repo. Nothing on GitHub holds it any more, so a session on a second account could not get it back. Second, as you asked: pictures on pages built by make_page.py break once a page is published or opened anywhere else. The builder copies each picture into a folder beside the page, named <page>-pics, and links it by a relative path. A published page carries only the HTML file, so the pictures are missing, which is why you keep seeing broken pictures in other repos. Third: three of your approvals for this page registered nothing. The page's Copy my reply box built your reply from the page's approval field. I had set that field to "Handoff overwrite" instead of "Design approved: Handoff overwrite", so the box gave you a line the design loop does not accept. The page builder only printed a note about it instead of refusing to build the page. The loop also rejects natural word orders such as "Handoff overwrite design approved 1A". This page's copy box is now fixed, so tapping it sends a line the loop accepts.
short.hint: Tap a row to see what it covers.
items: The save, the facts file and the pickup

The save runs after edits and at the end of each turn, writes a facts file (a short record of the branch, its commit and the uncommitted files) into the snapshot, and pushes it. The pickup fetches snapshots when a session starts. All of this stays; only where a snapshot is stored changes.

refs/house-rules/autosave/<branch> is shared by every folder on that branch. The newest save wins, whether or not it holds the older folder's work. The pickup also chose clone B's own newer local snapshot over clone A's snapshot on GitHub, which is why the second desktop session in clone B was offered nothing.
Pictures live in a folder beside the page

copy_pictures in scripts/make_page.py (line 149) copies each picture into <page>-pics/ and points the page at it. Publishing sends only the .html, and a page that is moved, previewed or opened from another repo also loses the folder. The same builder runs in every repo with the plugin, so the fix reaches all of them on the next update.
Approvals that look right register nothing

make_page.py (check_approval, line 347) still builds a page whose approval field is not a phrase the loop accepts, and only prints a note. The loop (design_loop.py, line 391) accepts only "Design approved: <feature>", with the stage words first, so a reply like "<feature> design approved 1A" changes nothing.
Three questions: saves, pictures and approvals
Question 1 asks how to keep each folder's saves apart, question 2 how pictures travel with a page, and question 3 how approvals are made to always register.
Choose one option in each question.

choices: q1
1. How are saves from different folders kept apart?
A
Each folder saves under its own name: refs/house-rules/autosave/<branch>/<folder id>

The folder id is a random id written once into that folder's .git directory. A save only ever replaces its own folder's snapshot. The pickup lists every snapshot for the current branch that holds files this folder lacks, newest first, each with its own restore command. Old snapshots pile up on GitHub until someone removes them. The save could delete its own snapshot once its folder has nothing uncommitted.
B
One place per branch, but a save refuses to replace a snapshot holding work it lacks

Before pushing, the save fetches the current snapshot and compares it with this folder. If the snapshot holds files this folder doesn't have, the save is skipped and prints one line saying so. Nothing is lost, but the second folder's own work stays unsaved on GitHub until the first folder's work is committed.
C
One place per branch, each save stacked on the one before it

Each new snapshot keeps the previous one as a second parent, so older saves stay reachable from the newest. The pickup walks back through the chain to find work this folder lacks. Nothing is lost and there is one name per branch, but the chain grows with every save, so the pickup gets slower and its output harder to read.
Each option keeps the restore command fix from commit d62be1a.
q2
2. How do pictures travel with a page?
A
Each picture is written into the page file itself

The builder reads each picture and writes its contents straight into the HTML as a data: address (the picture stored as text inside the page), so the page is one self-contained file. It shows its pictures when published, previewed, moved, emailed or opened from any repo. The page gets bigger by roughly a third more than the pictures' own size; a published page can be at most 16 MB, and the builder refuses a bigger one with a message naming the largest pictures. The <page>-pics folder is no longer written.
B
Keep the folder, and publish it beside the page

The builder keeps writing <page>-pics/, and every publish must also send that folder as the page's extra files. Published pages work, but a page opened from disk elsewhere, previewed, or published by a session that forgets the folder still loses its pictures.
A is the only option where nothing can forget to bring the pictures along.
q3
3. How are approvals made to always register?
A
The builder refuses pages whose reply would not register, and the loop accepts the stage words before or after the feature name

The builder refuses to build a design or plan page whose copy box would send a line the loop rejects, and names the fix. A page for another repo's work (#309) is still allowed, but only when the page names that repo in a field such as "forRepo": "owner/name". The loop also accepts "<feature> design approved <picks>" and "<feature> build plan approved". A test runs the copy-box line of every page through the loop's own check, so the two cannot disagree without the test failing.
B
Only the builder check
The builder refuses a page whose reply would not register, but a reply typed by hand in another word order still moves nothing.
A fixes both ways an approval can go wrong: a page offering a line the loop rejects, and a person typing a natural word order the loop rejects.

wrapup.summary: A design that stops a second folder erasing saved work, makes page pictures always show, and makes approvals always register.
